title: `when/then/otherwise`, `&`, `|`, `coalesce`: every operand runs on every row
verdict: no short-circuit: a raising branch raises on rows its condition excludes
description: The `when` docstring warns that Polars computes all expressions passed to `when-then-otherwise` in parallel and filters afterwards, so each expression must be valid on its own, whatever the conditions; its examples add that `when-then` always executes all expressions.

Most Polars arithmetic does not raise (integer division by zero gives NULL, integer overflow wraps: polars-int-divide, polars-int-arith), so the raising expressions are strict casts (polars-cast-int, polars-cast-double-to-int, polars-cast-string), string parsing and temporal errors (polars-temporal-errors). A `pl.when(c).then(x.cast(t))` therefore raises on a row `c` excludes when `x` does not fit `t`. The test of #29799 shows one exception the engine takes care of: a strict cast after masking a struct field succeeds only because masking nulled the field in every chunk.

The `coalesce` page says it folds left to right keeping the first non-null value, and is silent on whether later arguments run on the rows already decided. `&` and `|` are column operations; the docs do not say they short-circuit.

Leads: crates/polars-expr/src/expressions/ternary.rs, the `coalesce` kernel in crates/polars-ops, and py-polars/tests/unit/functions/test_when_then.py; probes of a strict cast in a `then` branch and in a later `coalesce` argument, in memory and streaming.
reference: The reference evaluates an expression only on the rows its operator sees: a `CASE` branch on the rows that reach it, a filter's condition on the rows below it, a join condition on the pairs it forms. Its issue analysis (`Rel.HasIssue`, `SubstraitLean/Safety.lean`; docs/how-it-works.md) trusts the engine's evaluation order: `CASE` is lazy, `AND`/`OR` are not, and filter and join conditions may run before the filters below them. A plan `verify` reports error-free must run without error, so an engine that evaluates a raising expression on rows outside that model breaks the guarantee. sverify's Polars translation would need its `CASE` written so that a raising branch only sees its rows, or the issue analysis to treat Polars's `CASE` as eager.

evidence.note: #29799: strict cast after masking a struct field
